certs.name: CERT Polska
certs.about: One of three national CSIRTs under Poland's National Cybersecurity System Act (with CSIRT GOV and CSIRT MON). Handles incidents for citizens, businesses, and most of the .pl space. Runs the national Warning List of phishing domains that Polish ISPs block, the SMS 8080 scam-text channel, and a large portfolio of open-source security tools.
certs.constituency: Citizens, private sector, local government, .pl domain and Polish IP space (except areas covered by CSIRT GOV and CSIRT MON)

services.name: Incident reporting form
services.desc: Online form for anyone in Poland to report phishing, fraud, malware or attacks.

services.name: SMS 8080
services.desc: Forward suspicious text messages free of charge to 8080. Reports feed SMS blocking by mobile operators.

services.name: Dangerous Websites Warning List
services.desc: 24/7-maintained list of phishing and scam domains. Polish ISPs block the domains at the DNS level. Entries stay on the list for six months.

services.name: Warning List data files
services.desc: Free downloads in text, JSON, XML, hosts, AdBlock, MikroTik and RPZ formats. CERT Polska recommends refreshing every 5 minutes.

services.name: Warning List check
services.desc: Tests whether your current connection is protected by the Warning List.

services.name: Warning List tools
services.desc: Scripts for deploying the list on Active Directory DNS, Pi-hole and other resolvers.

services.name: n6
services.desc: Free platform that sends organisations security events matched to their IP ranges and domains, from sinkholes, MWDB, Artemis and partners.

services.name: Artemis scanner
services.desc: Modular vulnerability scanner. CERT Polska runs it at scale against public-sector assets and privately reports findings to administrators.

services.name: MWDB
services.desc: Community malware repository with REST API. A free account gives access to samples and extracted configs.

services.name: Open-source portfolio
services.desc: mwdb-core, Karton, mquery (YARA search), malduck, DRAKVUF Sandbox, n6, Artemis.

services.name: Publications & warnings
services.desc: Threat analyses, vulnerability disclosures and scam campaign warnings in Polish and English.

services.name: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure
services.desc: CVE Numbering Authority. Coordinates vulnerabilities in Polish products and publishes advisories.

services.name: Annual report 2025
services.desc: Published 8 April 2026. Incident statistics, campaigns, and the Warning List in numbers.

stats.label: Incidents handled by CSIRT NASK in 2025
stats.note: +152% year on year, reported by Polskie Radio from a Ministry of Digital Affairs report

stats.label: Share of incidents that were fraud or social engineering (2025)

related.name: CSIRT GOV
related.desc: Government and critical infrastructure, run by the Internal Security Agency (ABW).

related.name: CSIRT MON
related.desc: Defence sector, Ministry of National Defence.

related.name: CSIRT KNF
related.desc: Sectoral team for financial market operators.

why.adv: Regular public warnings, analyses and monthly CSIRT NASK summaries on cert.pl.
why.feeds: Warning List published at hole.cert.pl/domains/v2 in TXT, CSV, JSON, XML, hosts and RPZ formats, plus an API.
why.block: Warning List is applied at DNS level by major Polish ISPs (Orange, Plus, Play, T-Mobile) under a UKE/ministry agreement and used by Quad9 and NextDNS.
why.report: Citizens can forward SMS to 8080, use the incydent.cert.pl web form, email cert@cert.pl, or report through mObywatel.
why.oss: Maintains open-source Artemis, MWDB Core, Karton and warning-list tools on GitHub.
why.proactive: Artemis scans over 500k domains and sends automated vulnerability emails; n6 distributes threat data to network owners.
why.transparency: Annual reports (2025 report published April 2026) and monthly incident summaries.
why.english: Full English site (cert.pl/en) and an English annual report.

certs.name: CERT.at
certs.about: Austria's national CSIRT. Known for its daily German-language security digest, automated notifications to Austrian network owners, and co-creating the open-source IntelMQ feed-processing tool. Also runs the Austrian Energy CERT and supports GovCERT Austria.
certs.constituency: Austrian internet users, companies and network operators

services.name: Warnings
services.desc: Public warnings on critical vulnerabilities and active campaigns.

services.name: Daily summary (Tageszusammenfassung)
services.desc: Free daily mailing list with a curated summary of security news and advisories.

services.name: RSS & Atom feeds
services.desc: Feeds for warnings, the blog and the daily summary.

services.name: Data feeds / emails from us
services.desc: Automated notifications to Austrian network owners about infected or vulnerable systems.

services.name: IntelMQ
services.desc: Open-source tool for collecting and processing threat feeds, co-created with CERT.PT and used by many CSIRTs.

services.name: Annual reports (Jahresbericht)
services.desc: Yearly reports on incidents and the Austrian threat landscape.

services.name: Report an incident
services.desc: Email reports@cert.at.

related.name: GovCERT Austria
related.desc: Government CERT, operated with the Federal Chancellery.

related.name: Austrian Energy CERT
related.desc: Sector CERT for the energy industry.

why.adv: Regular public warnings and blog posts, plus a daily digest ('Tagesberichte').
why.feeds: RSS/Atom feeds for the blog, warnings and the daily digest; no public IoC or CSAF data was found.
why.block: No public blocking service found.
why.report: reports@cert.at accepts incident reports; consumer scam reporting is mainly handled elsewhere (no citizen-oriented channel confirmed).
why.oss: Maintains open-source IntelMQ (certtools), tuency, intelmq-docker and the stats portal.
why.proactive: Systematically notifies Austrian network owners of vulnerable or infected systems via IntelMQ-driven processing.
why.transparency: Annual 'Bericht Internet-Sicherheit Österreich' (2020 to 2024 found; 2025 not yet seen).
why.english: An English site exists, but many warnings are in German only.

certs.name: CCB / CERT.be
certs.host: Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (Prime Minister's office)
certs.about: National CSIRT and NIS2 authority. Runs Safeonweb for the public, the suspect@safeonweb.be phishing inbox, the Belgian Anti-Phishing Shield with ISPs, and free tailored early warnings for registered organisations through Safeonweb@work.
certs.constituency: All of Belgium: citizens, organisations, essential and important entities

services.name: Advisories & warnings
services.desc: Warnings on critical vulnerabilities with patch guidance.

services.name: suspect@safeonweb.be
services.desc: Forward suspicious emails. The CCB extracts links and attachments and blocks malicious URLs. About 10 million messages were received in 2023.

services.name: Belgian Anti-Phishing Shield (BAPS)
services.desc: Phishing URLs reported by the public are redirected to a warning page by participating ISPs.

services.name: Safeonweb@work
services.desc: Free service where organisations register domains and IP addresses to receive tailored early warnings.

services.name: Safeonweb
services.desc: Public awareness site and app with alerts about current scams.

services.name: Report an incident
services.desc: Incident notification for organisations and NIS2 entities.

why.adv: ccb.belgium.be/advisories has dozens of paginated public 'Warning' advisories, with entries through late 2025.
why.feeds: An advisory RSS feed exists (used by the OpenCTI connector), but no public IoC, CSAF or API data was found.
why.block: The Belgian Anti-Phishing Shield (BAPS) with Proximus, Telenet, Orange and Belnet redirects the public away from reported malicious domains at ISP level.
why.report: Citizens forward suspicious messages to suspicious@safeonweb.be (over 9 million in 2024).
why.oss: It offers free closed tools and services such as the Safeonweb app; no open-source portfolio was found.
why.proactive: The Spear Warning programme proactively alerts companies and individuals about vulnerabilities, stolen credentials and malware.
why.transparency: Yearly statistics are published (suspicious@ volumes, BAPS clicks prevented, for example 13M in 2022).
why.english: Site and advisories are available in English alongside FR/NL/DE.

certs.full: Bulgarian Computer Security Incidents Response Team
certs.about: National CSIRT since 2008 and the NIS2 CSIRT for Bulgaria. Mostly serves state administration bodies. Trusted Introducer accredited since 2009. Publishes advisories in Bulgarian and runs training.
certs.constituency: Ministries, state agencies, national and regional administration

services.name: Security advisories
services.desc: Advisories and news for the public administration, in Bulgarian.

services.name: Report an incident
services.desc: Email cert@govcert.bg, weekdays 08:00–18:00.

services.name: Training
services.desc: Training on information security and incident management for the public sector.

why.adv: The govcert.bg warnings category has 2026 entries (Ghost-Sender, an email threat campaign), but the cadence appears irregular.
why.feeds: Public RSS feed of news and warnings (https://www.govcert.bg/feed/), confirmed by this site's feed collector in October 2026; no API, IoC or CSAF data found.
why.block: No blocking service found.
why.report: cert@govcert.bg in business hours; the constituency is state administration.
why.oss: No tools found.
why.proactive: Processes abuse alerts covering thousands of IPs (e.g. 5,100 IPs in a month), implying forwarding to owners, but the scope is unclear.
why.transparency: Monthly newsletters with incident statistics were reported by BTA; the current cadence is unverified.
why.english: An /en/ section exists, but content is largely in Bulgarian.

certs.name: CERT.hr
certs.about: Handles incidents involving the .hr domain or Croatian IP space, plus significant incidents in banking, financial infrastructure and digital infrastructure. Offers several free services, including a spam filter, a CVE subscription service and a web-shop checker.
certs.constituency: .hr domain, Croatian IP space, regulated sectors (state bodies are covered by ZSIS)

services.name: Warnings & recommendations
services.desc: Warnings on scam campaigns, such as those impersonating HZZO or the Interior Ministry, plus security recommendations.

services.name: CERT CVE

services.name: CERT spamblok
services.desc: Free spam-reduction service for users in Croatia.

services.name: PiXi
services.desc: Platform for mandatory incident reporting by regulated sectors.

services.name: incident@cert.hr
services.desc: Email incident reports with logs, timestamps and IP addresses.

services.name: Web-shop checker
services.desc: Tool to check whether an online shop looks fraudulent.

related.name: ZSIS CERT
related.desc: CERT for state administration bodies, at the Information Systems Security Bureau.

why.adv: Publishes security notices and recommendations; frequency not confirmed for 2026 (medium confidence).

why.block: No blocking service found.

why.oss: None found.

why.transparency: Annual reports (e.g. 2020, 2022) with figures.
why.english: Some English pages (e.g. phishing reporting), but mostly Croatian.

certs.about: National CSIRT launched in June 2018 with ITU support. Focuses on critical information infrastructure and operators of essential services. Publishes alerts and coordinates incidents.

services.name: Alerts & news

services.name: Report an incident

why.block: No blocking service found.
why.report: Only a general contact (info@csirt.cy) found; no citizen hotline or form found.
why.oss: None found.
why.proactive: No evidence of notifications to network owners.

why.adv: Publishes news and warnings, but no evidence of a regular advisory series.
why.feeds: The CZ.NIC Turris Sentinel greylist of attacker IPs is publicly available and reused by others (e.g. CESNET NERD).
why.block: Free downloadable Sentinel greylist and CSIRT.CZ deny lists for automated blocking.
why.report: National team handling incidents for all of Czechia; accepts reports from anyone, including phishing reports.
why.oss: The parent CZ.NIC maintains a major open-source portfolio (Knot DNS/Resolver, BIRD, FRED, Turris); CSIRT.CZ has its own Malicious Domain Manager.
why.proactive: Actively detects and removes phishing in .cz (down 80% in 2024) and notifies operators; scan-based notifications not fully verified.
why.transparency: Annual CSIRT.CZ report (2024) and a CZ.NIC annual report section.
why.english: Partial English content; CZ.NIC blog in English.

certs.name: SAMSIK / CFCS
certs.full: Styrelsen for Samfundssikkerhed (national CSIRT) and Center for Cybersikkerhed
certs.host: Danish Agency for Societal Security (Ministry for Societal Security and Preparedness); CFCS stays under the Defence Intelligence Service

CFCS, under the Defence Intelligence Service, keeps the operational defensive work, including the sensor network that monitors traffic at connected authorities and companies.
certs.constituency: Danish authorities, critical infrastructure, companies connected to the sensor network

services.name: Warnings (varsler)
services.desc: Public warnings about vulnerabilities and active threats.

services.name: Threat assessments
services.desc: National cyber threat assessment and current threat levels.

services.name: Sensor network

services.name: Report an incident

services.name: Sikkerdigital.dk

why.block: No evidence of blocking.

why.oss: No open-source tools found.

why.transparency: Annual 'cyber threat against Denmark' assessments and sector assessments (2024 CFCS, Nov 2025 SAMSIK).

certs.full: CERT-EE, Incident Response Department of RIA
certs.about: National CSIRT inside RIA. Publishes a monthly overview of incidents in Estonian cyberspace and an annual cyber security yearbook. It restricts access to scam and phishing sites and takes them down through hosts and partners.
certs.constituency: All of Estonia

services.name: Monthly cyberspace overview
services.desc: Monthly count of incidents with impact, with notable campaigns.

services.name: Phishing site blocking
services.desc: Restricts access to scam and phishing sites and notifies hosting providers.

services.name: cert@cert.ee
services.desc: Forward suspicious emails and report incidents.

services.name: Itvaatlik.ee
services.desc: Public awareness portal from RIA.

services.name: Cyber Security in Estonia yearbook
services.desc: Annual review of incidents and threats. The 2026 edition reviews 2025, a record year for fraud and for vulnerabilities.

stats.label: Incidents with impact in a single month (Sep 2024)

why.adv: Warnings appear occasionally via RIA news (e.g. Log4j, MikroTik); no regular advisory series was found.
why.feeds: Public RSS feed of news and warnings (https://www.ria.ee/en/rss-feeds/rss.xml), confirmed by this site's feed collector in October 2026; no API, IoC or CSAF data found.
why.block: A free CERT-EE DNS-filtering app for iOS/Android blocks phishing and malware domains for the public, and CERT-EE restricts access to malicious sites.
why.report: The public is asked to forward suspicious emails to cert@cert.ee.

why.proactive: Automated monitoring finds infected devices and notifies owners via telcos (e.g. 1,204 devices) and flags vulnerable hosts (e.g. 130 Cisco IOS XE devices).

why.english: Monthly reports and news are published in English.

certs.name: NCSC-FI
certs.about: National CSIRT known for clear public communication: a weekly review, a monthly Cyber Weather report, colour-coded alerts, and RSS and email subscriptions. Runs the Autoreporter service, which notifies Finnish network owners about infections, and the HAVARO detection system for critical organisations.
certs.constituency: All of Finland

services.name: Alerts
services.desc: Red alerts call for immediate action, yellow for caution.

services.name: Vulnerabilities
services.desc: Vulnerability notices with guidance.

services.name: Weekly review
services.desc: Weekly digest of cyber phenomena relevant to Finland.

services.name: Cyber Weather
services.desc: Monthly summary of the threat landscape.

services.name: Email subscriptions
services.desc: Subscribe to alerts, vulnerabilities and the weekly review by email.

services.name: Autoreporter
services.desc: Automated notifications to Finnish network operators about infected hosts and vulnerabilities.

services.name: HAVARO
services.desc: Detection system for critical organisations.

services.name: Report an incident
services.desc: Online form for citizens and organisations.

why.adv: Public vulnerability bulletins, weekly reviews and 'Information Security Now!' articles appear regularly (e.g. 3 critical bulletins in March 2026 alone).
why.feeds: RSS exists for Information Security Now! articles; vulnerability summaries go by email list; no IoC, CSAF or API found.
why.block: Traficom measures (protected SMS sender IDs, operator blocking of spoofed calls) protect the public, but no NCSC-run domain blocklist or protective DNS was found.
why.report: A public reporting page (kyberturvallisuuskeskus.fi/ilmoita) accepts reports of scams and incidents from anyone.
why.oss: Only the historic AbuseHelper co-development was found (old evidence); no current open-source portfolio.
why.proactive: Autoreporter has run for 20+ years and passes malware-traffic findings on Finnish networks to telcos, who notify customers.
why.transparency: There is a monthly 'Kybersää' (Cyber Weather) report plus an annual review (2025 review published).
why.english: There are substantial English pages (weekly reviews, reporting, RFC2350), though some products such as Kybersää are Finnish-first.

services.name: Alertes

services.name: ANSSI open source

services.name: Panorama de la cybermenace

services.name: Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr
services.desc: Victim assistance, diagnostics and referrals for citizens, SMEs and local authorities. Runs the 17Cyber platform.

related.name: Regional CSIRTs (CSIRT territoriaux)

why.transparency: Annual Panorama de la cybermenace (2025 edition published March 2026).
why.english: Has an English RFC2350 and some English reports, but most advisories are in French.

why.english: BSI has English pages, but WID advisories are mainly in German.
